deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down; it must be rotated 180 degrees to be read. The large circled word 'Runge' is a separate pencil inscription, unrelated to the mathematics. It is probably a name noted on a reused sheet, perhaps the mathematician C. Runge, but this cannot be determined. The ink notes are only scratch work, and several readings below are tentative.

(a) A heading reads roughly 'Try ∫_0^∞ x^{n-1}/φ(x) dx'. This proposes a Mellin-type integral of 1/φ(x) for some unspecified function φ. Nothing further about φ is written.

(b) There is a hand sketch of a smooth monotone curve, read here as decreasing. Its ends are marked '0' and '∞', and an arrow is labelled 'a' and '1'. This looks like a picture of a probability/tail function falling from 1 toward 0, with a cut-off point a marked.

(c) Gaussian normalisations, in my reading of the inverted symbols. The one confident constant is √(2/π):
  (1/√(2π)) ∫_{-∞}^{∞} e^{-x²/2} dx = 1, equivalently √(2/π) ∫_0^∞ e^{-x²/2} dx = 1.
  A further fragment pairs 1/√(2π) with e^{-x²/2} or e^{a²/2}. Together with the marked point a, this suggests he is setting up the normal tail probability (1/√(2π)) ∫_a^∞ e^{-x²/2} dx. It may also be the scaled tail (Mills ratio) e^{a²/2} ∫_a^∞ e^{-x²/2} dx. Ramanujan treated that quantity elsewhere, in the notebooks, via Laplace's continued fraction.
  These last identifications are my interpretation; the page contains no derivation, only these fragments.

The page has no connection to the q-series on the neighbouring pages (Rogers–Ramanujan material). It appears to be a reused or wrapper sheet.
errors: No derivation is carried far enough to contain an error.
The normalisation √(2/π)∫_0^∞ e^{-x²/2}dx = 1 is correct, if that is what is written.
The machine transcription's 'e^{-x²/a}' and leading '1/√π' are probably misreadings of 'e^{-x²/2}' / 'e^{a²/2}' and '1/√(2π)', caused by the inverted page.
